solution: By parts with \(u = x\), \(dv = \sin x\,dx\), so \(du = dx\), \(v = -\cos x\). Then \(\int x \sin x\,dx = -x\cos x + \int \cos x\,dx = -x\cos x + \sin x + C\).

By parts with \(u = x\), \(dv = \sin 3x\,dx\), so \(v = -\tfrac{1}{3}\cos 3x\). Then \(\int x \sin 3x\,dx = -\tfrac{x}{3}\cos 3x + \tfrac{1}{3}\int \cos 3x\,dx = -\tfrac{x}{3}\cos 3x + \tfrac{1}{9}\sin 3x + C\).

By parts with \(u = x^2\), \(dv = e^x\,dx\): \(\int x^2 e^x\,dx = x^2 e^x - 2\int x e^x\,dx\). Since \(\int x e^x\,dx = x e^x - e^x\), we get \(\int x^2 e^x\,dx = x^2 e^x - 2(x e^x - e^x) = e^x(x^2 - 2x + 2) + C\).

Take \(u = \log x\) (ILATE), \(dv = x\,dx\), so \(v = \tfrac{x^2}{2}\). Then \(\int x \log x\,dx = \tfrac{x^2}{2}\log x - \int \tfrac{x^2}{2}\cdot\tfrac{1}{x}\,dx = \tfrac{x^2}{2}\log x - \tfrac{1}{2}\int x\,dx = \tfrac{x^2}{2}\log x - \tfrac{x^2}{4} + C\).

Take \(u = \log 2x\), \(dv = x\,dx\), so \(du = \tfrac{1}{x}\,dx\), \(v = \tfrac{x^2}{2}\). Then \(\int x \log 2x\,dx = \tfrac{x^2}{2}\log 2x - \int \tfrac{x^2}{2}\cdot\tfrac{1}{x}\,dx = \tfrac{x^2}{2}\log 2x - \tfrac{x^2}{4} + C\).

Take \(u = \log x\), \(dv = x^2\,dx\), so \(v = \tfrac{x^3}{3}\). Then \(\int x^2 \log x\,dx = \tfrac{x^3}{3}\log x - \int \tfrac{x^3}{3}\cdot\tfrac{1}{x}\,dx = \tfrac{x^3}{3}\log x - \tfrac{1}{3}\int x^2\,dx = \tfrac{x^3}{3}\log x - \tfrac{x^3}{9} + C\).

Take \(u = \sin^{-1} x\), \(dv = x\,dx\), so \(v = \tfrac{x^2}{2}\). Then \(\int x \sin^{-1} x\,dx = \tfrac{x^2}{2}\sin^{-1} x - \tfrac{1}{2}\int \tfrac{x^2}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}\,dx\). Writing \(x^2 = 1-(1-x^2)\), \(\int \tfrac{x^2}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}\,dx = \sin^{-1} x - \int \sqrt{1-x^2}\,dx = \sin^{-1} x - \big(\tfrac{x}{2}\sqrt{1-x^2} + \tfrac{1}{2}\sin^{-1} x\big)\). Hence \(\int x \sin^{-1} x\,dx = \tfrac{2x^2-1}{4}\sin^{-1} x + \tfrac{x}{4}\sqrt{1-x^2} + C\).

Take \(u = \tan^{-1} x\), \(dv = x\,dx\), so \(v = \tfrac{x^2}{2}\). Then \(\int x \tan^{-1} x\,dx = \tfrac{x^2}{2}\tan^{-1} x - \tfrac{1}{2}\int \tfrac{x^2}{1+x^2}\,dx\). Since \(\int \tfrac{x^2}{1+x^2}\,dx = \int\big(1 - \tfrac{1}{1+x^2}\big)dx = x - \tan^{-1} x\), we get \(\int x \tan^{-1} x\,dx = \tfrac{1}{2}(x^2+1)\tan^{-1} x - \tfrac{x}{2} + C\).

Take \(u = \cos^{-1} x\), \(dv = x\,dx\), so \(v = \tfrac{x^2}{2}\), \(du = -\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}\,dx\). Then \(\int x \cos^{-1} x\,dx = \tfrac{x^2}{2}\cos^{-1} x + \tfrac{1}{2}\int \tfrac{x^2}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}\,dx\). Using \(\int \tfrac{x^2}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}\,dx = \tfrac{1}{2}\sin^{-1} x - \tfrac{x}{2}\sqrt{1-x^2}\), we get \(\int x \cos^{-1} x\,dx = \tfrac{x^2}{2}\cos^{-1} x + \tfrac{1}{4}\sin^{-1} x - \tfrac{x}{4}\sqrt{1-x^2} + C\).

Take \(u = (\sin^{-1} x)^2\), \(dv = dx\), \(v = x\): \(\int (\sin^{-1} x)^2\,dx = x(\sin^{-1} x)^2 - 2\int \tfrac{x\sin^{-1} x}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}\,dx\). For the remaining integral take \(u = \sin^{-1} x\), \(dv = \tfrac{x}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}\,dx\), \(v = -\sqrt{1-x^2}\): \(\int \tfrac{x\sin^{-1} x}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}\,dx = -\sqrt{1-x^2}\,\sin^{-1} x + \int 1\,dx = -\sqrt{1-x^2}\,\sin^{-1} x + x\). Therefore \(\int (\sin^{-1} x)^2\,dx = x(\sin^{-1} x)^2 + 2\sqrt{1-x^2}\,\sin^{-1} x - 2x + C\).

[Textbook answer-key error: NCERT key prints the last term as (+x); the correct antiderivative is (-x), verified by differentiation of (-sqrt{1-x^2}cos^{-1}x-x).] Take \(u = \cos^{-1} x\), \(dv = \tfrac{x}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}\,dx\), so \(v = -\sqrt{1-x^2}\) and \(du = -\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}\,dx\). Then \(\int \tfrac{x\cos^{-1} x}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}\,dx = -\sqrt{1-x^2}\,\cos^{-1} x - \int \big(-\sqrt{1-x^2}\big)\big(-\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}\big)dx = -\sqrt{1-x^2}\,\cos^{-1} x - \int 1\,dx = -\sqrt{1-x^2}\,\cos^{-1} x - x + C\).
Take \(u = x\), \(dv = \sec^2 x\,dx\), so \(v = \tan x\). Then \(\int x \sec^2 x\,dx = x\tan x - \int \tan x\,dx = x\tan x - (-\log|\cos x|) = x\tan x + \log|\cos x| + C\).

Write \(\tan^{-1} x = 1\cdot\tan^{-1} x\) and take \(u = \tan^{-1} x\), \(dv = dx\), \(v = x\). Then \(\int \tan^{-1} x\,dx = x\tan^{-1} x - \int \tfrac{x}{1+x^2}\,dx = x\tan^{-1} x - \tfrac{1}{2}\log(1+x^2) + C\).

Take \(u = (\log x)^2\), \(dv = x\,dx\), so \(v = \tfrac{x^2}{2}\), \(du = \tfrac{2\log x}{x}\,dx\). Then \(\int x(\log x)^2\,dx = \tfrac{x^2}{2}(\log x)^2 - \int x \log x\,dx\). Using \(\int x \log x\,dx = \tfrac{x^2}{2}\log x - \tfrac{x^2}{4}\), we get \(\int x(\log x)^2\,dx = \tfrac{x^2}{2}(\log x)^2 - \tfrac{x^2}{2}\log x + \tfrac{x^2}{4} + C\).

Take \(u = \log x\), \(dv = (x^2+1)\,dx\), so \(v = \tfrac{x^3}{3} + x\). Then \(\int (x^2+1)\log x\,dx = \big(\tfrac{x^3}{3} + x\big)\log x - \int \big(\tfrac{x^3}{3} + x\big)\tfrac{1}{x}\,dx = \big(\tfrac{x^3}{3} + x\big)\log x - \int \big(\tfrac{x^2}{3} + 1\big)dx = \big(\tfrac{x^3}{3} + x\big)\log x - \tfrac{x^3}{9} - x + C\).
This has the form \(\int e^x\big[f(x) + f'(x)\big]dx = e^x f(x) + C\) with \(f(x) = \sin x\), \(f'(x) = \cos x\). Hence \(\int e^x(\sin x + \cos x)\,dx = e^x \sin x + C\).

Write \(\tfrac{x}{(1+x)^2} = \tfrac{(1+x)-1}{(1+x)^2} = \tfrac{1}{1+x} - \tfrac{1}{(1+x)^2}\), so the integrand is \(e^x\big[f(x)+f'(x)\big]\) with \(f(x) = \tfrac{1}{1+x}\), \(f'(x) = -\tfrac{1}{(1+x)^2}\). Hence \(\int \tfrac{x e^x}{(1+x)^2}\,dx = \tfrac{e^x}{1+x} + C\).

Using \(1+\cos x = 2\cos^2\tfrac{x}{2}\) and \(1+\sin x = 1 + 2\sin\tfrac{x}{2}\cos\tfrac{x}{2}\), \(\tfrac{1+\sin x}{1+\cos x} = \tfrac{1}{2}\sec^2\tfrac{x}{2} + \tan\tfrac{x}{2}\). So the integrand is \(e^x\big[f(x)+f'(x)\big]\) with \(f(x) = \tan\tfrac{x}{2}\), \(f'(x) = \tfrac{1}{2}\sec^2\tfrac{x}{2}\). Hence \(\int e^x\Big(\tfrac{1+\sin x}{1+\cos x}\Big)dx = e^x \tan\tfrac{x}{2} + C\).
This is \(\int e^x\big[f(x) + f'(x)\big]dx\) with \(f(x) = \tfrac{1}{x}\), \(f'(x) = -\tfrac{1}{x^2}\). Hence \(\int e^x\big(\tfrac{1}{x} - \tfrac{1}{x^2}\big)dx = \tfrac{e^x}{x} + C\).
Using \(\int e^{ax}\sin bx\,dx = \tfrac{e^{ax}}{a^2+b^2}(a\sin bx - b\cos bx) + C\) with \(a = 2\), \(b = 1\): \(\int e^{2x}\sin x\,dx = \tfrac{e^{2x}}{5}(2\sin x - \cos x) + C\).

Put \(x = \tan\theta\), so \(\tfrac{2x}{1+x^2} = \sin 2\theta\) and \(\sin^{-1}\big(\tfrac{2x}{1+x^2}\big) = 2\theta = 2\tan^{-1} x\) (for \(-1\le x\le 1\)). Then \(\int \sin^{-1}\big(\tfrac{2x}{1+x^2}\big)dx = 2\int \tan^{-1} x\,dx = 2\big(x\tan^{-1} x - \tfrac{1}{2}\log(1+x^2)\big) = 2x\tan^{-1} x - \log(1+x^2) + C\).

Using \(1+\cos 2x = 2\cos^2 x\) and \(\sin 2x = 2\sin x\cos x\), \(\tfrac{2+\sin 2x}{1+\cos 2x} = \tfrac{2 + 2\sin x\cos x}{2\cos^2 x} = \sec^2 x + \tan x\). So the integrand is \(e^x\big[f(x)+f'(x)\big]\) with \(f(x) = \tan x\), \(f'(x) = \sec^2 x\). Hence \(\int \tfrac{2+\sin 2x}{1+\cos 2x}e^x\,dx = e^x \tan x + C\).

Put \(x = \cos 2\theta\); then \(\tfrac{1-x}{1+x} = \tfrac{1-\cos 2\theta}{1+\cos 2\theta} = \tan^2\theta\), so \(\tan^{-1}\sqrt{\tfrac{1-x}{1+x}} = \theta = \tfrac{1}{2}\cos^{-1} x\). Thus \(\int \tan^{-1}\sqrt{\tfrac{1-x}{1+x}}\,dx = \tfrac{1}{2}\int \cos^{-1} x\,dx\). Since \(\int \cos^{-1} x\,dx = x\cos^{-1} x - \sqrt{1-x^2}\), the answer is \(\tfrac{1}{2}\big(x\cos^{-1} x - \sqrt{1-x^2}\big) + C\).

Using \(1-\cos x = 2\sin^2\tfrac{x}{2}\) and \(1-\sin x = 1 - 2\sin\tfrac{x}{2}\cos\tfrac{x}{2}\), \(\tfrac{1-\sin x}{1-\cos x} = \tfrac{1}{2}\operatorname{cosec}^2\tfrac{x}{2} - \cot\tfrac{x}{2}\), which is \(f(x)+f'(x)\) with \(f(x) = -\cot\tfrac{x}{2}\), \(f'(x) = \tfrac{1}{2}\operatorname{cosec}^2\tfrac{x}{2}\). So \(\int e^x\big(\tfrac{1-\sin x}{1-\cos x}\big)dx = -e^x\cot\tfrac{x}{2}\). Evaluating, \(\int_{\pi/2}^{\pi} e^x\big(\tfrac{1-\sin x}{1-\cos x}\big)dx = \big[-e^x\cot\tfrac{x}{2}\big]_{\pi/2}^{\pi} = -e^{\pi}\cot\tfrac{\pi}{2} + e^{\pi/2}\cot\tfrac{\pi}{4} = 0 + e^{\pi/2} = e^{\pi/2}\).

By parts with \(u = x\), \(dv = e^x\,dx\): \(\int x e^x\,dx = x e^x - \int e^x\,dx = e^x(x-1)\). Hence \(\int_{0}^{1} x e^x\,dx = \big[e^x(x-1)\big]_{0}^{1} = e^1(0) - e^0(-1) = 0 - (-1) = 1\), as required.

By parts with \(u = \sin^{-1} x\), \(dv = dx\), \(v = x\): \(\int \sin^{-1} x\,dx = x\sin^{-1} x - \int \tfrac{x}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}\,dx = x\sin^{-1} x + \sqrt{1-x^2}\). Hence \(\int_{0}^{1} \sin^{-1} x\,dx = \big[x\sin^{-1} x + \sqrt{1-x^2}\big]_{0}^{1} = \big(1\cdot\tfrac{\pi}{2} + 0\big) - \big(0 + 1\big) = \tfrac{\pi}{2} - 1\), as required.
